# C10 — Underused Language Primitives

*Level 1 card. 6 root causes. Open the level-2 card before accepting any of them.*

Energy waste from not using available optimized language features, standard library functions, or runtime-specific constructs that would accomplish the same task more efficiently. This includes manually reimplementing functionality available as C-optimized built-ins (skipping built-ins), choosing a less efficient built-in when a faster one exists (inefficient choice), using per-element loops when bulk/vectorized primitives exist (missing bulk usage), building strings via repeated concatenation instead of join (inefficient string building), placing variables in scopes with unnecessary lookup overhead (inefficient scope), and using operators on custom types that trigger expensive dunder methods (hidden operator overloads).

## Root causes in this category

| ID | Name | The repair | Measurable? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **C10.S1** | Skipping Optimized Built-ins | call the builtin instead of the loop | yes, scales with input |
| **C10.S2** | Inefficient Built-in Choice | swap in the faster equivalent | yes, scales with input |
| **C10.S3** | Missing Bulk Primitive Usage | use the bulk or vectorised primitive | yes, scales with input |
| **C10.S4** | Inefficient String Concatenation | collect the parts in a local list and join once, so the accumulator that grows is never the aliased one | yes, scales with input |
| **C10.S5** | Inefficient Scope Lookup | alias the global to a local before the loop | yes, scales with input |
| **C10.S6** | Expensive Operator Overloads | call the underlying operation directly, or work on primitives in the loop | yes, scales with input |

Card paths: `reference/root-causes/C10.S1.md`, `reference/root-causes/C10.S2.md`, `reference/root-causes/C10.S3.md`, `reference/root-causes/C10.S4.md`, `reference/root-causes/C10.S5.md`, `reference/root-causes/C10.S6.md`

## Telling this category from its neighbours

These come up often enough to check before you commit:

- **C10.S1 vs C3.S1 Inefficient Iteration Construct** — Ask whether a loop still exists afterwards.  C10.S1 removes it entirely. C3.S1 keeps it and changes its form (index-based to direct, loop to comprehension).
- **C10.S2 vs C4.S8 Non-Idiomatic Condition** — C10.S2 replaces a hand-written form with the primitive that already exists (`in dict`, `dict.get`).  C4.S8 is about the *branch structure* around a lookup, not about which lookup form is used.  If the repair deletes a branch, it is C4.S8; if it swaps one expression for a shorter equivalent, it is C10.S2.
- **C10.S5 vs C8.S3 Missing Local Lookup Caching** — C10.S5 is about *scope* -- a global or builtin whose cost is the LEGB walk.  C8.S3 is about an *attribute chain* whose cost is repeated dict lookups.  Same repair shape, different thing being resolved.

## If nothing here fits

Say so and move on. Reporting a weak match from an already-open category is the most common way this analysis goes wrong: the category is open because a static signal pointed at it, not because a smell is there.
